name: Chicken with 40 Cloves of Garlic
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Source lists 419 cal / 25g protein using 2 lb boneless thighs; est 600 plated with potatoes - confidence medium on calories. Shortest ingredient list in the whole slice (garlic is the recipe), so it is the cheapest per serving. NEAR-DUPE WATCH vs the live Chicken Scampi, which is also garlic-forward but lemon-butter over pasta. | HARVEST:
intro_html: This is a five ingredient French classic and one of them is garlic in an amount that makes people laugh when they read it. Do not be alarmed. Whole cloves braised slowly in broth turn sweet, mild, and creamy, nothing like the sharp bite of raw or minced garlic. The name is a promise rather than a limit, and scaled up to feed fourteen you are going to be peeling for a while. Each bowl carries {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein for about ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost).
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 4.75 lb (2117 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh, 4.75 lb: ~$8.26. Buy 5 lbs: $8.85.
Chicken Broth, 2.25 cups: ~$0.75. Buy 1 (covers this batch with some left over).
Rice, 6.25 cups dry: ~$1.41. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 2lb bags.
Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper, ground cumin, dried dill, dried thyme): ~$0.28. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $18.31 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.31 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $19.09 across 14 servings, roughly $1.36 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $18.66 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $37.75. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost), and the shortest ingredient list in the entire batch. Chicken, garlic, olive oil, broth, and rice. That is the whole recipe, and it tastes like far more than the sum of it.
shop_smart: Buy whole heads of garlic, not the peeled tubs or the jarred minced. Whole heads are cheaper by a wide margin, they keep for weeks on the counter, and peeled garlic that has been sitting in liquid will not give you the sweet, creamy result this dish depends on.
Smash each clove lightly with the flat of a knife and the skin slips right off. That trick turns a tedious job into a ten minute one, which matters a lot at this quantity.
Boneless thighs are the cheap cut and the correct one. There is very little else in this pot, so the chicken has to stay juicy on its own.
With only five real ingredients, quality actually shows. Use a decent olive oil here, since there is nothing else in the pan to hide behind.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Peel all the garlic. Smash each clove with the flat of a knife first and the skins come off easily. Keep the cloves whole.
Season the chicken thighs with salt, pepper, cumin, thyme, and dill and brown them in the olive oil in batches until deeply colored. Set them aside.

Turn the heat down to medium-low, add all the garlic to the pan, and cook it slowly for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until the cloves turn golden and soft. Burnt garlic will ruin the entire pot, so low and slow is the only setting here.
Pour in the chicken broth and scrape the bottom of the pan clean, then return the chicken with any juices.
Cover and simmer 30 minutes until the chicken is tender and the garlic cloves have collapsed into the sauce.
Uncover and simmer 10 more minutes to reduce, mashing a few cloves against the side of the pan to thicken the sauce naturally.
Cook the rice and taste for salt before you portion.
portion_html: Weigh the rice into each container, then set the pan on the scale, subtract the empty weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. Make sure the soft garlic cloves get spread around, since they are the best part and it would be a shame for one container to get all of them. Every portion lands at {{cal}} calories.

recipeIngredient: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh, 4.75 lb (2117 g)
steps: Peel all the garlic, keeping the cloves whole.
Season and brown the chicken thighs in olive oil, then set aside.
Cook the whole garlic cloves slowly over medium-low heat until golden and soft.
Add the broth, return the chicken, cover, and simmer 30 minutes.
Uncover and reduce 10 minutes, mashing some cloves into the sauce.
Cook the rice and weigh both into 14 containers.
